Write and run `/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/test/server.test.mjs` (node:test + node:assert/strict, Node v22, built-ins only, no npm install). Load skill tdd-workflow if available. Project rules: small functions (<50 lines), file under ~600 lines, no console.log, deterministic tests, every test cleans up its child process and temp dir (use t.after / try-finally with `stop()` and `removeDir`). Use EXACT equality for every spec value (never regex/prefix for bodies, headers, stderr lines).

Read first: the spec `/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/.team/notes/spec.md` (Server section + API persistence lines), `/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/.team/notes/backend-api.md`, the server `/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/server.mjs`, and the shared harness `/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/test/support/harness.mjs` (exports makeTempDir, removeDir, startServer({cwd, env}) -> {port, child, stdout(), stderr(), stop(), exited()}, runToExit({cwd, env}) -> {code, stdout, stderr}, request(port,{method,path,headers,body}), postBooking(port, obj|string, headers?), rawRequest, parseRaw, JSON_TYPE). Import it as `./support/harness.mjs`. Do NOT edit server.mjs or the harness; if the harness has a bug, report it to me with the fix you'd make (you may add a small local helper in your test file instead).

Data file layout: `{"nextId": N, "bookings": [{id,room,title,date,start,end},...]}`. A valid booking: `{room:'Aurora',title:'Standup',date:'2026-11-03',start:'09:00',end:'10:00'}`.

Tests to write (one `test()` or subtest each):
Startup / PORT
1. Stdout is exactly `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>\n` with the real port (harness checks the regex; also assert stdout() equals that exact string after a few requests incl. errors and a 500 — stdout never gets anything else).
2. PORT invalid -> runToExit: code 1, stdout '', stderr is exactly one line (ends with '\n', contains exactly one '\n', length > 1) — message text free. Cases: 'abc', '-1', '+80', ' 80', '80 ', '8.0', '1e3', '٣٠٠٠' (Arabic-Indic digits), '０' (fullwidth), '65536', '99999999999999999999', '0x10'.
3. PORT valid boundary: '0' starts; '00000' starts (digits only, value 0). '65535' — don't bind it; skip that.
4. Unset PORT and empty PORT mean 3000: do NOT bind 3000 for real (may be in use). Instead: occupy port 3000 yourself? No — instead verify by startup order trick: with PORT unset/empty AND an invalid data file, the server must print `cannot read data file x.json` (proving PORT passed the check). Assert exact stderr `cannot read data file x.json\n`, code 1. Optionally, if `net.createServer().listen(3000,'127.0.0.1')` succeeds in the test, hold it, then start server with PORT unset and a valid temp DATA_FILE -> expect exit 1 with one stderr line (port in use proves it tried 3000); same with PORT=''. If 3000 cannot be grabbed (already in use by someone else), the server also must exit 1 — either way assert code 1 & one stderr line & stdout ''.
5. Port in use: grab an ephemeral port with net server on 127.0.0.1, start server with PORT=<that port> -> code 1, stdout '', one stderr line.
6. Startup order: invalid PORT + invalid data file -> stderr is NOT `cannot read data file ...` (PORT checked first). Invalid data file + port in use -> stderr exactly `cannot read data file <name>\n` (data read before listen).
Data file
7. Each of these -> code 1, stdout '', stderr exactly `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>\n`, and the file content unchanged afterwards: path is a directory; ENOTDIR (DATA_FILE='afile/data.json' where afile is a regular file); empty file; whitespace only; 'not json'; 'null'; '[]'; '{}'; '{"nextId":1}'; UTF-8 BOM + valid layout; a booking with an extra key; nextId not greater than an id; duplicate ids; a booking with invalid date. Use a relative DATA_FILE in some cases (e.g. 'data/b.json') so `<name>` is the relative name as given, and an absolute one in another (name is the absolute path as given). Also a DATA_FILE with a trailing './' segment like './x.json' must appear as './x.json'.
8. DATA_FILE unset and empty -> uses `bookings.json` in cwd: put an invalid `bookings.json` in the temp cwd -> stderr exactly `cannot read data file bookings.json\n`. Then with a valid `bookings.json` containing one booking in cwd, start with DATA_FILE unset -> GET /api/bookings shows it.
9. ENOENT: missing file -> starts with no bookings, and the file is NOT created at startup nor after GETs/404/405/400/409/415 requests. Missing parent folder -> also starts with no bookings, and the folder is not created.
10. Relative DATA_FILE resolved against cwd, not server.mjs folder: cwd = temp dir, DATA_FILE='sub/data.json' with sub created; POST -> file appears at <tmp>/sub/data.json and NOT under the repo dir.
11. A seeded valid file (2 bookings, nextId 7) loads: GET shows them; next POST gets id 7.
Persistence
12. POST twice (ids 1,2), DELETE 2, stop, restart same DATA_FILE: bookings equal [booking 1]; next POST gets id 3 (never reused). Also delete all bookings then restart -> next id continues.
13. The file is written before the reply: right after the 201 reply (no wait), read the file and it contains the booking; right after 204, it no longer contains it.
14. Outside changes not noticed: after start, overwrite the file with other content; GET still shows memory state; and a later POST rewrites the file from memory.
15. No write on other requests: after a POST, record file mtimeMs+content; then send GET /api/rooms, GET /api/bookings, GET /, GET /app.js, invalid POSTs (400, 409, 413, 415), DELETE /api/bookings/999 (404), 405s; wait ~50ms; assert content AND mtimeMs unchanged. Startup with an existing file doesn't rewrite it (mtime unchanged after start + GETs; set an old mtime with fs.utimes before start to make it robust).
Save failure
16. DATA_FILE='missing/data.json' (folder absent): POST valid -> 500, body `{"error":"internal error"}` exactly (parse & deepEqual), Content-Type exactly JSON_TYPE; server still running (exited() false, GET /api/rooms 200); GET /api/bookings -> []; folder still absent. Then create the folder, POST again -> 201 with id 1 (next id unchanged).
17. Save failure on DELETE: start with a seeded file in a temp sub folder, then remove the folder (rm -r), DELETE /api/bookings/1 -> 500 internal error; GET still shows booking 1; recreate folder; DELETE -> 204.
Concurrency
18. Send 10 overlapping POSTs at once (Promise.all; same room/date, different overlapping times like 09:00-10:00, 09:30-10:30, ...): exactly one 201, nine 409 each with body error `room is already booked from <s> to <e>` naming the created booking's times; GET shows one booking. Then 10 non-overlapping POSTs at once: all 201, ids distinct and = 2..11 as a set; file on disk equals memory after restart.
Body draining
19. POST with Content-Type text/plain and a 5 MB body -> client receives 415 `content type must be application/json` (use request()). POST with JSON type and 5 MB body -> 413 `body too large`. Also on the same keep-alive socket: use rawRequest-like net socket writing two pipelined requests (first a 2 MB-body 415 POST with Content-Length, then `GET /api/rooms` with Connection: close) and assert both replies arrive (status lines 415 then 200).
20. A 500 from save failure keeps the server alive for further requests (covered in 16) and stderr may receive diagnostics, but stdout stays only the listening line.

Then run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5 && node --test test/server.test.mjs` and make it pass. If a test fails because server.mjs violates the spec (not a test bug), do NOT change server.mjs and do not weaken the test: leave it, and report the failing test name, observed vs expected and the spec line. Report: file path, test count, pass/fail output summary, any suspected server bugs.

content.content: 1 # Full task spec (verbatim from the user — final, no questions possible) 2 3 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). 4 5 Server 6 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 7 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 8 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 9 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 10 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 11 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 12 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 13 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. I wrote the test file, but I couldn't run it. The Bash tool was denied permission, so `node --test test/server.test.mjs` never ran and nothing has been verified.

**File:** `/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/test/server.test.mjs`, about 440 lines. It has roughly 53 tests: 12 bad-PORT cases, 2 good-PORT cases, 16 unusable-data-file cases and the rest one each. The count is from the file layout, not from a run.

**Coverage:** all 20 items in your list.
- Item 4 is split into "PORT unset/empty passes the PORT check" and "PORT unset/empty means 3000". The 3000 test tries to hold 3000 itself and carries on if that fails.
- Items 13 and 15 read the file right after the reply.
- Item 15 sets a fixed old mtime with `utimes` and compares `mtimeMs`.
- Item 20 is folded into the first test. It sends requests including a 500 from a save failure, then checks stdout is exactly the listening line.

**Things to know:**
- **`tdd-workflow` skill:** it doesn't exist in this environment, so I skipped it.
- **Server and harness:** I changed neither, and I found no harness bug.
- **Last assertion (pipelined test):** the final assertion in the pipelined-socket test calls `parseRaw` twice and is clumsy. It is correct but could be tidied.
- **Suspected server bug:** I found none reading `server.mjs` against the spec.
- **Possible failure (700 Hz `utimes`):** I didn't check whether `mtimeMs` after `utimes` is exactly stable on this filesystem. If it isn't, that comparison may need adjusting.

To finish, I need Bash permission to run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5 && node --test test/server.test.mjs`. Alternatively, you can run it and send me the failures. I'll then fix any test bugs and report real server violations without touching `server.mjs`.
